title: Long Freeze Cycle
shortDescription: Freeze cycle exceeded the maximum allowed time.
fullDescription:
The Indigo/NXT controller flags E01 when the freeze cycle takes longer than the programmed maximum (typically 60 minutes). This indicates poor heat rejection, low refrigerant charge, or insufficient water flow over the evaporator. The machine will retry several times before locking out.

Common causes include a dirty condenser, weak compressor, or a faulty thermistor reading low evaporator temperature. Verify ambient and water temperatures are within spec before condemning components.

causes.cause: Dirty air-cooled condenser restricting heat rejection
Low refrigerant charge or restriction in TXV
Weak compressor or failing start components

fixSteps.title: Clean condenser coil
fixSteps.instruction: Power off, vacuum and brush the condenser fins. Verify intake and exhaust clearances meet spec.

fixSteps.title: Verify water inlet temperature
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm incoming water below 90 F (32 C). High water temp extends freeze cycle.

fixSteps.title: Check refrigeration pressures
fixSteps.instruction: Connect gauges to access ports and compare suction/discharge to nameplate values. Refrigerant work requires EPA certification.

whenToCallPro: Refrigerant diagnosis and repair require an EPA-certified commercial technician.
videoSearchQuery: Manitowoc Indigo NXT E01 long freeze fix

faq.q: Will cleaning the condenser fix E01?
faq.a: Often yes. A blocked condenser is the single most common cause and routine cleaning prevents recurrence.

title: Long Harvest Cycle
shortDescription: Harvest cycle exceeded its maximum time limit.
fullDescription:
E02 is set when the harvest cycle (hot-gas defrost releasing the ice slab) runs longer than the maximum allowed time, typically 3.5 minutes. The control expects the harvest thermistor to reach a setpoint indicating the slab has dropped.

Likely causes are a stuck hot-gas valve, low water levels preventing release, scaled evaporator, or a misreading harvest thermistor.

causes.cause: Hot-gas solenoid valve not opening fully

fixSteps.title: Descale the evaporator
fixSteps.instruction: Run an approved nickel-safe ice machine cleaner cycle following Manitowoc procedure.

fixSteps.title: Inspect water curtain
fixSteps.instruction: Verify curtain swings freely and the magnetic switch reads correctly.

fixSteps.title: Test hot-gas valve
fixSteps.instruction: Verify 24V at coil during harvest and listen for valve opening. Replace if stuck.

whenToCallPro: Hot-gas valve replacement requires refrigerant recovery by certified personnel.

faq.a: Every 6 months minimum, more often in hard water areas.

title: Thin Ice Detection
shortDescription: Ice slab is too thin at end of freeze.
fullDescription: The control compares the ice thickness probe contact time against the freeze setpoint. If ice is too thin for several cycles, E03 is set. Causes include poor water distribution, scaled evaporator, low water flow, or an out-of-adjustment thickness probe.

causes.cause: Restricted water inlet or low pressure

fixSteps.title: Clean and descale
fixSteps.instruction: Run cleaning cycle with Manitowoc cleaner and sanitizer per manual.

fixSteps.title: Adjust thickness probe
fixSteps.instruction: Set gap to specification (typically 3/16 inch) using factory procedure.

fixSteps.title: Verify water supply
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm inlet pressure 20-80 psi and clean inlet strainer.

whenToCallPro: Persistent thin ice after cleaning suggests refrigeration or pump issues for a tech.
videoSearchQuery: Manitowoc E03 thin ice probe adjustment

faq.q: Can I adjust the probe myself?
faq.a: Yes, the procedure is in the operator manual and requires basic tools.

title: Water Sensor Fault
shortDescription: Water level/probe sensor reading invalid.
fullDescription:
E04 indicates the water level probe or sump sensor is reporting an out-of-range condition. The control cannot confirm proper sump fill before starting a freeze cycle. The unit will halt to prevent dry running of the pump.

Common causes are scale buildup on the probe, a disconnected harness, or a failed water inlet valve preventing fill.

fixSteps.title: Clean water probe
fixSteps.instruction: Remove probe and descale with Manitowoc cleaner. Reinstall and verify clean tip.

fixSteps.title: Test inlet valve
fixSteps.instruction: Energize valve and confirm water flow into sump. Replace if no flow at 24V.

whenToCallPro: Control board diagnostics require service tech with schematics.
videoSearchQuery: Manitowoc E04 water sensor fault fix

faq.q: Why does the probe scale up so fast?
faq.a: Hard water deposits accumulate quickly. Use a water filter to extend probe life.

title: High Condenser Temperature
shortDescription: Condenser temperature exceeded safe limit.
fullDescription: The Indigo NXT monitors condenser inlet/outlet temperature. If readings exceed safe operating limits, E05 is set and the machine shuts down to protect the compressor. Causes include dirty condenser, blocked airflow, high ambient, or fan failure on air-cooled units; for water-cooled units it can be loss of cooling water.

causes.cause: High ambient temperature in equipment room
Loss of water flow on water-cooled units

fixSteps.title: Clean condenser thoroughly
fixSteps.instruction: Power off, brush and vacuum coil. Wash with coil cleaner if heavily soiled.

fixSteps.title: Test condenser fan
fixSteps.instruction: Verify fan runs during freeze cycle. Check capacitor and motor amperage.

fixSteps.title: Check ambient and clearances
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm ambient under 100 F and 6 inch minimum clearances.

whenToCallPro: If condenser is clean and fan operates, refrigeration diagnosis is needed.

faq.a: Every 3 months in normal kitchens, monthly in greasy environments.

title: Slow Water Fill
shortDescription: Sump did not fill to setpoint within allowed time.
fullDescription: E07 is set when sump water does not reach the upper probe within the allotted fill time. Causes include closed/restricted water supply, clogged inlet strainer, weak inlet valve, or air locks. Some units allow continued operation but throw a warning.

fixSteps.title: Inspect supply
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm shutoff fully open, replace 5-micron prefilter if installed.

fixSteps.title: Clean inlet screen
fixSteps.instruction: Remove inlet hose, clean strainer at solenoid valve.

whenToCallPro: If pressure is adequate and screens are clean, the inlet valve likely needs replacement.

faq.a: Manitowoc specifies 20-80 psi dynamic pressure.

title: Bin Full / Bin Switch Active
shortDescription: Ice level switch indicates bin full or sensor stuck.
fullDescription: When the bin thermostat or paddle/eye sensor detects a full bin, the unit pauses production. If displayed when the bin is not actually full, the bin switch may be misadjusted, iced over, or failed. NXT models use a thermistor; older Indigo uses a mechanical switch.

causes.cause: Iced or stuck mechanical bin switch

fixSteps.title: Clear bin
fixSteps.instruction: Remove ice down to below sensor and confirm normal operation.

fixSteps.title: Inspect sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Check for ice, debris, or damaged wires at the bin switch/thermistor.

fixSteps.title: Test thermistor
fixSteps.instruction: Measure resistance against Manitowoc temp/resistance chart, replace if out of spec.

whenToCallPro: If sensor reads correctly but code persists, control board may need service.

faq.a: Mounted on the lower front of the ice machine head, behind the front panel.

title: Cleaning Reminder

fullDescription: Indigo NXT tracks runtime and water usage to remind operators to perform cleaning and sanitizing. The CLEAN indicator does not stop production but should be addressed promptly to avoid scaling and bacterial buildup that lead to other faults.

fixSteps.title: Sanitize

faq.a: No. Skipping cleaning leads to scale, slime, and harvest faults.

title: Compressor Discharge Temperature High
shortDescription: Compressor discharge sensor exceeded safety limit.
fullDescription: E08 indicates the discharge line thermistor reached a temperature that risks compressor damage. Frequent causes are low refrigerant charge, compressor mechanical wear, blocked condenser, or non-condensables in the system.

fixSteps.title: Clean condenser
fixSteps.instruction: Eliminate easy causes first by deep-cleaning the condenser coil.

fixSteps.title: Refrigeration diagnosis

title: Water Pump Fault
shortDescription: Water recirculation pump not running or drawing wrong amperage.
fullDescription: E09 is reported when the controller does not see expected feedback from the recirculation pump or detects abnormal current draw. Without the pump, water cannot flow over the evaporator, leading to thin ice and harvest issues.

fixSteps.title: Inspect pump
fixSteps.instruction: Check pump impeller for debris and shaft for free rotation.

fixSteps.title: Test motor
fixSteps.instruction: Measure winding resistance and supply voltage. Replace pump if open or shorted.

whenToCallPro: If a new pump still throws E09, the control board needs evaluation by a technician.

faq.q: Can I clean the pump instead of replacing?
faq.a: Sometimes. Scale and debris can mimic failure; clean first, then test.

title: Refrigeration High-Pressure Lockout
shortDescription: High-pressure switch tripped.
fullDescription: The high-pressure cutout opened, indicating discharge pressure above safe operating limits. The control locks out the compressor to prevent damage. Causes mirror E05 and E08: dirty condenser, fan failure, overcharge, or non-condensables.

fixSteps.title: Reset and observe
fixSteps.instruction: After cleaning condenser, cycle power and watch for repeat trip.

fixSteps.title: Pressure diagnosis
fixSteps.instruction: Certified tech connects gauges and verifies subcooling, charge, and switch operation.

whenToCallPro: High-pressure issues are refrigeration faults that require certification.

faq.a: Most HP switches auto-reset, but the control will lock out after repeated trips.

title: Communication Error
shortDescription: Loss of communication between control board and display.
fullDescription: E12 indicates the user interface and main control are not communicating. Causes include damaged ribbon cable, loose connectors, water intrusion, or a failed board. The unit cannot run reliably until communication is restored.

fixSteps.title: Reseat connectors
fixSteps.instruction: Power off, disconnect and reconnect ribbon cable and harnesses on both boards.

fixSteps.title: Inspect for moisture
fixSteps.instruction: Dry any water intrusion and locate the source (often a leaking water line).

whenToCallPro: Board replacement and harness diagnosis warrant a technician.

faq.q: Can a power surge cause E12?
faq.a: Yes. Surges can damage one or both boards; a surge protector is recommended.

title: Water Pump Failure
shortDescription: Water recirculation pump not running or drawing wrong current.
fullDescription:
E23 indicates the Indigo NXT controller detects the water pump is either not energizing or pulling outside its expected current band. Without water recirculation across the evaporator, ice cannot form properly and the freeze cycle will fail.

The controller monitors pump current via the relay board. Common failures are seized pump impeller from scale, bad capacitor, or wiring fault to the pump motor.

fixSteps.title: Power down and inspect pump
fixSteps.instruction: Turn off the unit at the disconnect. Remove the splash shield and inspect the pump for visible scale or debris.

fixSteps.title: Descale and free impeller
fixSteps.instruction: Run a Manitowoc-approved descaler cycle. Manually rotate impeller to confirm free movement.

fixSteps.title: Test pump motor
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect pump leads and meter winding resistance against service manual values. Replace pump if open or shorted.

whenToCallPro: If wiring or relay testing is required, call a refrigeration technician.
videoSearchQuery: Manitowoc Indigo NXT E23 water pump replace

faq.q: Can scale really stop the pump?
faq.a: Yes. Hard water deposits can lock the impeller within months if descaling is skipped.

title: Float Switch Stuck
shortDescription: Water reservoir float switch not changing state during fill.
fullDescription:
E24 is logged when the reservoir float switch fails to open or close as expected during the fill cycle. The control needs to see the switch transition to confirm proper water level for ice making.

Usually caused by mineral buildup gluing the float in place, but can also indicate a wiring break or failed reed switch.

fixSteps.title: Inspect and clean float
fixSteps.instruction: Lift the float and verify it slides freely on its stem. Clean with descaler if sticky.

fixSteps.title: Test switch continuity
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect leads and check continuity in both float positions with a multimeter.

fixSteps.title: Replace float assembly
fixSteps.instruction: Install OEM float assembly if switch is faulty.

whenToCallPro: Replace if cleaning does not restore proper switching.

faq.q: Why does my float keep sticking?
faq.a: Hard water minerals coat the float stem; descale every 6 months to prevent recurrence.

title: Bin Thermistor Open/Short
shortDescription: Bin temperature sensor reading out of range.
fullDescription:
E25 fires when the bin thermistor reads outside its valid resistance range, suggesting an open circuit or shorted sensor. The bin thermistor in NXT models monitors storage temperature for ice quality reporting.

A failed sensor will not stop ice making but disables certain bin diagnostics until cleared.

fixSteps.title: Reseat connector
fixSteps.instruction: Verify the bin thermistor plug is fully seated on the control board.

fixSteps.title: Measure resistance
fixSteps.instruction: Read thermistor resistance at room temperature; compare against service manual table (typically 10kΩ at 25°C).

fixSteps.title: Replace thermistor
fixSteps.instruction: Swap in OEM bin thermistor and route harness clear of sharp edges.

whenToCallPro: Call a tech only if the control board appears to have a damaged input.

faq.q: Will ice production stop on E25?
faq.a: Usually no — ice still produces but bin diagnostics are unreliable until repaired.

title: Bin Empty Notification
shortDescription: Storage bin reports no ice present.
fullDescription:
BIN EMPTY is an informational message indicating the bin level sensor reports zero ice. Typically used by smart-monitoring systems or AuCS to alert staff that production cannot keep up.

If displayed during normal hours despite production, check curtain switch and bin sensor calibration.

fixSteps.title: Verify bin status visually
fixSteps.instruction: Open bin and confirm whether ice is actually depleted.

fixSteps.title: Check sensor alignment
fixSteps.instruction: If bin contains ice, realign the bin level sensor per service manual.

whenToCallPro: Rarely needs a pro; only if sensor electronics are suspect.

faq.a: No, it is informational unless the bin clearly has ice.

title: Bin Full Indicator (Repeated)
shortDescription: Bin reports full and machine entered standby.
fullDescription:
When the bin level switch / curtain / thermistor reports the bin is full, the controller stops ice production and shows BIN FULL. If this clears within minutes during dispensing, no action is needed.

Persistent BIN FULL despite empty bin indicates a stuck curtain switch or misadjusted bin thermostat.

fixSteps.title: Break ice bridge
fixSteps.instruction: Manually break any ice bridges that may be holding the curtain shut.

fixSteps.title: Test curtain switch
fixSteps.instruction: Operate curtain by hand and verify switch toggles correctly.

whenToCallPro: Replace bin thermostat or board only with a tech.

faq.q: Why does BIN FULL come on when bin is empty?
faq.a: Most often a curtain switch stuck closed or an ice bridge holding the curtain.

title: Cleaning Cycle Reminder (Repeated)
shortDescription: Programmed cleaning interval has elapsed.
fullDescription:
CLEAN appears at the user-set service interval (default 6 months) reminding the operator to run a cleaning cycle. Ignoring it leads to scale buildup and further faults like E01 and E02.

Use only Manitowoc-approved cleaner and sanitizer; vinegar damages nickel-plated evaporators.
